subject: Graph Theory and Network Algorithms
topic: Spanning Trees, Cut Property, and Kruskal's Algorithm with DSU
syllabus_context: Unit III: Trees and Spanning Forests. Free trees, spanning tree characterization, fundamental cycle property, cut property theorem, Kruskal's greedy algorithm, Disjoint Set Union (DSU) with union-by-rank and path compression, Prim's algorithm comparison, complexity bounds, minimum spanning forest extensions.
declared_learning_objective: Define spanning trees in connected undirected graphs, prove the Cut Property theorem, trace Kruskal's greedy algorithm using Disjoint Set Union data structures, compare asymptotic complexity with Prim's algorithm, and evaluate edge weight conditions and spanning forest limits.

provenance.source: Standard Academic Discrete Mathematics & Algorithms Lecture Series

recording_quality.known_observability_limitations: Graph diagrams, cut partitions (S, V-S), and DSU parent pointers drawn on blackboard and spoken aloud.
